questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means stop. You must come to a complete stop, let all traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: A primary cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes is:

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
Running off the road while avoiding another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning too wide in a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: A primary cause of single-vehicle crashes is turning too wide in a curve. This can cause a motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: When wearing a helmet during a crash, a rider is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than a person not wearing a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as a person not wearing a helmet.
More likely to survive than a person not wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than a person not wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked until your next stop.
Continue squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and immediately re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake pressure. Then re-apply the brake with controlled, gradual pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: The center portion of a lane has an oily strip. This strip:

options.text: Should be avoided at all times.
Usually provides good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should only be used if sharing the lane with another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily but provides good traction unless it rains. The strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can ride on either side and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmets every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: All curves are different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist ride in the lane?
questions.explanation: If being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation.

questions.question: A motorcycle should fit you. What does this mean?

options.text: Your fingertips should barely touch the handlebars when you sit on the motorcycle.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when you stand next to the motorcycle.
Your feet should touch the ground comfortably when you sit on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should touch the ground comfortably when you sit on the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet can touch the ground comfortably while you are sitting. Make sure your motorcycle fits you before you ride it.

questions.question: If you carry a load on your motorcycle, where should it be placed?

options.text: On the gas tank in front of you.
Stacked against the sissy bar or frame behind the seat.

questions.explanation: Place loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Get off and walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight across the tracks within your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride straight within your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your angle may push you into another lane and cause a crash with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, if you crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake pressure right away. Then apply the brake again with controlled, gradual pressure.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-fourths of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: As your motorcycle speeds up, what do you need to do?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle speeds up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: When you stop, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop. Make this a habit every time.

questions.question: _________ of crashes between motorcycles and cars are caused by car drivers not giving motorcyclists the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because car drivers do not give motorcyclists the right-of-way. Never assume that a car driver will yield to you, even if they are supposed to by law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should avoid obstacles on the road. If avoiding an obstacle is not possible, what should the motorcyclist do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat can cushion the impact.
Approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle and must ride over it, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: When riding near a truck, what should you know?

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists must avoid blind spots, especially on large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: The law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield provides the best protection.

questions.question: What should riders know about blind spots on motorcycles?

options.text: They are nothing to worry about.
They do not exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal routine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, pick one that:

options.text: Keeps you hidden from other drivers.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Keep a safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when starting the engine?
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the speedometer that comes on when the engine is on and in neutral.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Leather boots provide the best foot protection. Boots should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down and approach the dog, then quickly speed away as it gets close.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and approach the dog, then quickly speed away as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If you see a dog approaching, slow down and downshift. Quickly accelerate away as the dog approaches.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.
